reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence and holiday helpers, but distributes the daily skip-versus-move decision across shared scheduling, server handlers, and budget templates.

duplication.why: Daily-frequency dispatch is repeated across four consumers, with nearly identical filtering and adjustment pipelines in the two server handlers.

placement.why: Holiday classification belongs in shared/schedules.ts, but recurrence policy also appears in server handlers and budget-template orchestration.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the requested scheduling changes, their tests, configuration type, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate several implementations of daily skipping and different occurrence-search limits, while the new handler leaves config untyped despite the existing RecurConfig type.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange implement daily filtering outside applyWeekendRule, while createScheduleList computes frequency-dependent flags to selectively disable shared weekend handling.

disguised_duplication.where: The daily non-working-day policy is expressed as bounded search in getNextDate, filter/map pipelines in both server handlers, and frequency-dependent helper flags in createScheduleList.

abstraction_drift.where: Holiday support adds the getDateWithSkippedWeekend holidays parameter and WeekendRule.holidays option; getNextDate gains a daily-specific branch, while getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, and createScheduleList independently dispatch daily handling outside the shared weekend-rule abstraction.
